title: What to say when someone says 'I was only joking'
summary: This post explains how to handle rude remarks disguised as jokes using the 'Say It and Wait' technique. The creator suggests that responding with 'I don't think you were' and remaining silent calls their bluff and forces them to back down or double down.
key_points: When someone makes a rude remark and claims 'I was only joking,' it lets them have it both ways by insulting you while pretending they didn't.
Laughing it off makes you look like you can't take a joke, while being overly direct ('What's funny about that?') can feel combative.
Use the 'Say It and Wait' technique instead.
When they say 'I was just joking,' respond with: 'I don't think you were.'
Wait in silence for their response, even though it feels long and uncomfortable.
Not caving in forces them to call their bluff; they will either double down weakly or back off and apologize.
content: What to say when someone says 'I was only joking'. Here's what to say when someone makes a rude remark and then goes, I was just joking. You're at work or at an event, and someone oversteps. Watch out when she starts talking, it never stops. Or Maybe he'll finally decide to have an opinion today. Or, Hey, looks like you've been enjoying the snacks in the break room lately. When it's clear that you're not amused, they immediately say, Hey, I was only joking. But that lets them have it both ways. They said something rude, but they can pretend they didn't, and you're the one with a problem because you lack a sense of humor. I taught communication at Duke and Columbia for more than a decade and here is what to do. No one wants to look like they can't take a joke. So the temptation is to laugh it off and say it's fine. But if it was a joke, then they didn't really do anything wrong, and you know they did. The other move is to get really direct. What's funny about that? That does work, but it's a little combative, especially in front of other people. Instead, you can use what I call the Say It and Wait technique. When they say, Come on, I was just joking. You say, I don't think you were. And then you wait until they respond. It can feel very long, and it is uncomfortable, but that's the point. Here's why it works. If you don't cave in and start talking, they're going to have to say something eventually. You've called their bluff. They either have to double down, No, for real, I was just joking, which looks a little weak at that point. Or they're going to back off. Hey, look, it didn't land. Sorry. Either way, you've won because they were counting on the fact that they could hide behind the cover of a joke. But when you pull it away, it's obvious to everyone that they're being rude. So the next time someone tells you they were just joking, try the Say It and Wait technique. And follow me for more on becoming a better communicator.
